items.x: Delilah was paid by the Philistine lords to find out the secret of Samson's strength.

clues: I was the daughter of Eliam.
A king saw me from his roof while I was washing.
My first husband was a Hittite soldier who was sent to die in battle.
I went to King David to make sure my son Solomon would reign.
items.x: Bathsheba, wife of Uriah, later married David; she secured the throne for her son Solomon.

clues: I was the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Zidonians.
I fed hundreds of prophets of Baal at my table.
I wrote letters in the king's name to have Naboth stoned for his vineyard.
I painted my face and looked out of a window before I was thrown down.
items.x: Jezebel, Ahab's queen, promoted Baal worship, had Naboth killed, and died thrown from a window.

clues: My house was upon the town wall.
I hid two men under stalks of flax on my roof.
I let the spies down by a cord through the window.
A scarlet line in my window saved my family when the walls of Jericho fell.
items.x: Rahab hid Joshua's spies in Jericho, and she and her household were spared.

clues: I was an Egyptian handmaid.
An angel found me by a fountain of water on the way to Shur.
I called the LORD 'Thou God seest me.'
In the wilderness of Beersheba God showed me a well, and my son Ishmael was saved.
items.x: Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian maid, bore Ishmael and was twice met by God in the wilderness.

clues: An angel said I would be a wild man, with my hand against every man.
I was born when my father was eighty-six years old.
I was sent away with my mother after mocking at a feast for my younger brother.
I grew up in the wilderness of Paran and became an archer.
items.x: Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar, grew up in the wilderness and became an archer.

clues: I was a tiller of the ground.
God did not respect my offering of the fruit of the ground.
God told me, 'Sin lieth at the door.'
After I killed my brother, God set a mark upon me.
items.x: Cain, Adam's first son, killed his brother Abel and was marked by God.

clues: I was king of Salem.
I brought forth bread and wine to meet a man returning from battle.
Abraham gave me tithes of all.
The Psalms speak of a priest for ever after my order.
items.x: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, blessed Abram.

clues: Solomon made me ruler over the labour of the house of Joseph.
A prophet tore a new garment into twelve pieces and gave me ten.
I fled into Egypt until Solomon died.
I set up golden calves in Bethel and Dan.
items.x: Jeroboam became the first king of the northern kingdom and set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

clues: I lived in Jezreel, next to a king's palace.
I said, 'The LORD forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers.'
Two false witnesses accused me of blaspheming God and the king.
I was stoned so a king could take my vineyard.
items.x: Naboth refused to sell his vineyard to Ahab and was stoned after a plot by Jezebel.

clues: I was the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite.
I was angry because one Jew would not bow to me.
I cast lots, called Pur, to choose a day to destroy the Jews.
I was hanged on the gallows I made for Mordecai.
items.x: Haman plotted to destroy the Jews but was hanged on his own gallows.

clues: I was also called Didymus.
I was not with the other disciples when the risen Jesus first came to them.
I asked Jesus, 'How can we know the way?'
Eight days after the resurrection, Jesus told me to reach my hand into his side.
items.x: Thomas, called Didymus, doubted the resurrection until he saw the risen Jesus.

clues: Philip found me and told me about Jesus of Nazareth.
Jesus called me an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile.
Jesus said he saw me under the fig tree before Philip called me.
I said to Jesus, 'Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.'
items.x: Nathanael was brought by Philip and confessed Jesus as Son of God and King of Israel.

clues: Seven devils had gone out of me.
I ministered to Jesus with other women from my substance.
I stood by the cross of Jesus.
At the tomb I thought the risen Jesus was the gardener.
items.x: Mary Magdalene followed Jesus and was the first to see him risen.

clues: My sisters sent word to Jesus, 'Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.'
I had been in the grave four days.
I came out bound hand and foot with graveclothes.
The chief priests wanted to put me to death too, because many believed in Jesus because of me.
items.x: Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Mary and Martha, was raised from the dead after four days.

clues: I was coming out of the country into Jerusalem.
My sons were named Alexander and Rufus.
Soldiers compelled me to do a task as Jesus went to Golgotha.
I carried the cross of Jesus.
items.x: Simon, a man of Cyrene, was compelled to carry Jesus' cross.

clues: I was a notable prisoner.
I had been cast into prison for sedition and murder.
Pilate offered the crowd a choice between me and Jesus.
The crowd cried for me to be released.
items.x: Barabbas, a prisoner, was released instead of Jesus at the crowd's demand.

clues: My mother was a Jewess who believed, but my father was a Greek.
Paul circumcised me before taking me on his journeys.
My grandmother Lois and mother Eunice had unfeigned faith.
Paul told me, 'Let no man despise thy youth.'
items.x: Timothy, Paul's young helper, received two letters from him.

clues: My husband and I left Rome when Claudius commanded all Jews to depart.
We were tentmakers by trade, and Paul worked with us.
We took a gifted preacher aside and explained the way of God more perfectly.
With my husband Aquila I hosted a church in our house.
items.x: Priscilla and her husband Aquila were tentmakers who worked alongside Paul.

clues: Wise men from the east came to my city asking where the King of the Jews was born.
I sent them to Bethlehem and asked them to bring me word.
I was mocked when the wise men went home another way.
I ordered all the children in Bethlehem two years old and under to be killed.
items.x: Herod the king tried to destroy the infant Jesus and killed the children of Bethlehem.

clues: I had been the wife of Philip.
John the Baptist told the king it was not lawful for him to have me.
I had a quarrel against John and would have killed him.
I told my daughter to ask for John's head in a charger.
items.x: Herodias, wife of Herod Antipas, plotted the death of John the Baptist.

clues: I was threshing wheat by the winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
I pulled down my father's altar of Baal by night.
I asked God for a sign with a fleece of wool.
I defeated Midian with three hundred men, trumpets and lamps in pitchers.
items.x: Gideon tested God with a fleece and defeated Midian with three hundred men.

clues: I was a keeper of sheep.
I brought the firstlings of my flock as an offering.
God had respect unto me and to my offering.
Hebrews says that by faith, though I am dead, I still speak.
items.x: Abel offered a pleasing sacrifice and was killed by his brother Cain.

clues: I became king of Judah at sixteen and reigned fifty-two years.
I loved husbandry and had towers and cisterns built.
I went into the temple to burn incense, which only priests could do.
Leprosy rose up in my forehead, and I was a leper until I died.
items.x: King Uzziah prospered until pride led him to burn incense, and he was struck with leprosy.

clues: Believers prayed in my mother Mary's house the night Peter escaped.
I went with Paul and Barnabas, but left them at Perga and returned to Jerusalem.
Paul and Barnabas split over whether to take me again.
Later Paul wrote, 'He is profitable to me for the ministry.'
items.x: John Mark left Paul's first journey early, but later Paul called him profitable for ministry.

clues: I am mentioned in the shortest of Paul's letters.
In time past I was unprofitable to my master, but now profitable.
Paul begot me in his bonds and sent me back.
I was a runaway servant whose master, Philemon, was asked to receive me as a brother.
items.x: Onesimus, a runaway slave, became a believer through Paul and was sent back to Philemon.

items.q: The Bible says some people have entertained angels without knowing it.
items.x: 'Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.'

items.q: The name “Lucifer” appears many times in the book of Revelation.
items.x: In the KJV, 'Lucifer' appears only once, in Isaiah 14:12.

items.q: “God works in mysterious ways” is a Bible verse.
items.x: It's a line from a hymn by William Cowper. Isaiah says, 'My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways.'

items.q: Paul calls James the Lord's brother.
items.x: 'Other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord's brother.'

items.q: The chief priests had Jesus' tomb sealed and guarded by soldiers.
items.x: Pilate said, 'Ye have a watch.' They sealed the stone and set a watch.

items.q: The Bible says Adam and Eve had only two sons, Cain and Abel.
items.x: They also had Seth, and Adam 'begat sons and daughters'.

items.q: The Bible lists “seven deadly sins” by name.
items.x: There is no such list. Proverbs gives six things the LORD hates, 'yea, seven are an abomination unto him', but they are not the 'seven deadly sins'.

items.q: The Bible names the repentant thief on the cross as Dismas.
items.x: Luke never names either criminal. 'Dismas' comes from later legend.

items.q: Jesus said it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
items.x: Jesus said this after the rich young man went away sorrowful.

items.q: Moses parted the Jordan River so Israel could enter Canaan.
items.x: That was under Joshua: the priests stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan. Moses parted the Red Sea.

items.q: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him but a few days.
items.x: 'They seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.' He then served seven more years.

items.q: The Bible says an innkeeper turned Mary and Joseph away.
items.x: No innkeeper is mentioned. Luke says only that there was 'no room for them in the inn'.

items.q: The Bible says God will never give you more than you can handle.
items.x: The verse is about temptation: God 'will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able', and will make a way to escape.

items.q: Jesus prayed that his followers would be kept from the evil while still in the world, though they are not of the world.
items.x: 'I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.'

items.q: Joseph's brothers first planned to kill him, but Reuben persuaded them to throw him into a pit instead.
items.x: Reuben said, 'Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit,' hoping to rescue him later.

items.q: Solomon asked God for an understanding heart, and God also gave him riches and honour.
items.x: God said, 'I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour.'

items.q: In the KJV, Jesus says, “I am the bread of life.”
items.x: 'I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger.'

items.q: The Bible says Satan was cast out of heaven for refusing to bow to Adam.
items.x: That story is not in Scripture. Jesus said, 'I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.'

items.q: The Bible says the angels were singing when they appeared to the shepherds.
items.x: Luke says the heavenly host were 'praising God, and saying, Glory to God in the highest'. Carols added the singing.

items.q: King Saul came from the tribe of Judah.
items.x: Saul was a Benjamite, 'of the smallest of the tribes of Israel'. David was from Judah.

items.q: Absalom cut his hair once a year because it grew so heavy.
items.x: 'At every year's end ... he polled it: because the hair was heavy on him.'

items.q: Ruth was the great-grandmother of King David.
items.x: Ruth bore Obed, 'the father of Jesse, the father of David'.

items.q: When God first called Jonah to Nineveh, he went straight there.
items.x: Jonah 'rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD'.

items.q: Jonah was overjoyed when God spared Nineveh.
items.x: 'It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.'

items.q: Daniel was thrown to the lions for refusing to bow to a golden image.
items.x: Daniel was thrown in for praying to God three times a day against the king's decree. The golden image was his three friends' test.

items.q: Esther was Mordecai's daughter.
items.x: She was 'his uncle's daughter', his cousin. Mordecai raised her as his own after her parents died.

items.q: Job's three friends sat with him in silence for seven days and seven nights.
items.x: 'None spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.'

items.q: At the end of Job's trials, the LORD gave him twice as much as he had before.
items.x: 'The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.'

items.q: In the parable of the prodigal son, the older brother happily joined the feast.
items.x: 'He was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.'

items.q: In the parable of the sower, Jesus explains that the seed is the word of God.
items.x: 'Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.'

items.q: The Bible says Jesus was crucified on a mountain called Mount Calvary.
items.x: Luke says 'the place, which is called Calvary'. The Gospels never call it a mountain.

items.q: Jesus ascended to heaven from the mount called Olivet, near Jerusalem.
items.x: After the ascension the apostles 'returned unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet'.

items.q: Paul was born a Roman citizen.
items.x: The chief captain bought his citizenship 'with a great sum'. Paul said, 'But I was free born.'

items.q: After his vision on the Damascus road, Saul was blind for three days.
items.x: 'He was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink.'

items.q: The book of Revelation was written by the apostle Paul.
items.x: It was given to 'his servant John', who was on the isle of Patmos.

items.q: Revelation says each gate of the holy city is a single pearl.
items.x: 'Every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold.'

items.q: Revelation describes a sea of glass like crystal before God's throne.
items.x: 'Before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal.'

items.q: “To thine own self be true” comes from the book of Proverbs.
items.x: It's from Shakespeare's Hamlet. Proverbs actually warns, 'Be not wise in thine own eyes.'

items.q: “Charity begins at home” is a Bible verse.
items.x: It's a proverb, not Scripture. Paul writes, 'Charity suffereth long, and is kind.'

items.q: Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died, and his eye was not dim.
items.x: 'His eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.'

items.q: Hannah prayed so earnestly in the temple that Eli thought she was drunk.
items.x: Her lips moved but her voice was not heard, 'therefore Eli thought she had been drunken'.

items.q: Elisha called down fire from heaven against the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
items.x: That was Elijah. The fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice after his prayer.

items.q: Moses broke the first tables of the ten commandments when he saw the golden calf.
items.x: 'He cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.'

items.q: The Bible says we should cast our bread upon the waters.
items.x: 'Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.'

items.q: Jesus' first disciples included two pairs of brothers.
items.x: Simon Peter and Andrew, then James and John, the sons of Zebedee.

items.q: Put these leaders of Israel in the order they judged.
items.x: Deborah (Judges 4), Gideon (Judges 6–8), Samson (Judges 13–16), then Samuel, the last judge, who anointed Saul.

items.q: Put these prophets in the order they ministered.
items.x: Samuel anointed Saul and David, Nathan served King David, Elijah confronted Ahab, and Elisha took up Elijah's mantle.

items.q: Put these events in David's life in order.
items.x: David was anointed as a boy, killed Goliath, spared Saul in the cave at Engedi, and was made king over Judah in Hebron after Saul died.

items.q: Put these plagues of Egypt in order.
items.x: Blood was the first plague, frogs the second, locusts the eighth, and the death of the firstborn the tenth.

items.q: Put these events in Elijah's life in order.
o: A still small voice at Horeb
items.x: Ravens fed him during the drought, fire fell at Carmel, he fled to Horeb and heard the still small voice, and finally he went up by a whirlwind.

items.q: Put these events in Abraham's life in order.
items.x: Abram left Haran at 75, Ishmael was born when he was 86, Isaac when he was 100, and then came the test on Moriah.

items.q: Put these events in Jacob's life in order.
o: Dreams of a ladder at Bethel
items.x: Jacob took the blessing, fled and dreamed at Bethel, served Laban for his wives, then wrestled at Peniel on his way home.

items.q: Put these events in Moses' life in order.
o: Hidden in an ark of bulrushes
items.x: Moses was hidden as a baby, fled to Midian after killing an Egyptian, met God at the bush, and led Israel through the sea.

items.q: Put these appearances of the risen Jesus in order.
items.x: Emmaus was on the day of the resurrection, Thomas saw him eight days later, then came the shore of Tiberias, and the ascension after forty days.

items.q: Put these kings in the order they appear in the book of Daniel.
items.x: Nebuchadnezzar took Daniel captive, Belshazzar saw the writing on the wall, Darius the Median took the kingdom, and Daniel's last vision came in the third year of Cyrus.

items.q: Put these events from Luke 1 in order.
items.x: Zacharias was told first in the temple. Six months later Gabriel came to Mary, who then visited Elisabeth before John was born.

items.q: Put these minor prophets in Bible order.
items.x: The minor prophets open Hosea, Joel, Amos, Obadiah, Jonah.

items.q: Put these poetry books in Bible order.
items.x: The poetry books run Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, then the Song of Solomon.

items.q: Put these events in Samson's life in order.
o: Sends foxes with firebrands into the corn
Tells a riddle at his wedding
items.x: The lion came first; later he found honey in its carcase, which became his wedding riddle. Then came the foxes, and much later Delilah.

items.q: Put these events from the book of Joshua in order.
o: Defeat at Ai because of Achan
items.x: Israel crossed the Jordan, took Jericho, lost at Ai because of Achan's sin, and later the sun stood still at Gibeon.

items.q: Put these kings of Judah in the order they reigned.
items.x: Rehoboam, Solomon's son, came first; Jehoshaphat reigned in Ahab's time; Hezekiah in the Assyrian crisis; Josiah near the end of the kingdom.

items.q: Put these events of the exile and return in order.
o: Daniel is cast into the lions' den
items.x: Nebuchadnezzar's army burnt the temple, Daniel faced the lions under Darius, the second temple was finished under Darius of Persia, and Nehemiah rebuilt the wall decades later.

items.text: But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our LORD: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.
For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.

For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.

I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.

For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.
And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.
And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.
And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.
And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:

And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.
But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day.
I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:
The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.
Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.

And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the LORD his God.

And Elisha prayed, and said, LORD, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.

And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested.

Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all.
So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.
My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.
O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD’s name is to be praised.
The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.
There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.
The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
A GOOD name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
And the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.
But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.
And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel.
The LORD hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.
It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.
Therefore I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me.
But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.
Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.

Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?
Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:

Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.

items.q: Why was Moses not allowed to lead Israel into the Promised Land?
o: He broke the first tables of stone
He struck the rock instead of speaking to it
items.x: God told Moses to speak to the rock. He smote it twice, and God said, 'Ye shall not bring this congregation into the land.'

items.q: Why did Jacob love Joseph more than all his other sons?
o: Joseph was the son of his old age
items.x: 'Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age.'

items.q: Samuel told Saul his kingdom would not continue. What had Saul done at Gilgal?
o: Offered the burnt offering himself instead of waiting
items.x: Tired of waiting for Samuel, Saul offered the burnt offering himself. Samuel said, 'Now thy kingdom shall not continue.'

items.q: Why did Joseph's ten brothers first travel down to Egypt?
o: To buy corn during the famine
items.x: 'Joseph's ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt,' for the famine was in the land of Canaan.

items.q: What reason did Jonah give God for running away to Tarshish?
o: He was afraid of the king of Nineveh
He did not believe God had spoken
He wanted to visit his family
He knew God was gracious and would spare Nineveh
items.x: 'I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger ... and repentest thee of the evil.'

items.q: Why did Herod go on to arrest Peter after he had killed James?
o: He saw that it pleased the Jews
items.x: Herod killed James with the sword, 'and because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.'

items.q: Why did God strike Uzzah dead as the ark was carried to Jerusalem?
o: He took hold of the ark when the oxen shook it
He stole gold from the ark
items.x: When the oxen shook the cart, Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark, 'and God smote him there for his error.'

items.q: Why were Paul and Silas beaten and jailed in Philippi?
o: They cast a spirit of divination out of a slave girl
They started a riot in the temple
items.x: Her masters lost their gain when Paul cast out the spirit, so they dragged Paul and Silas to the magistrates.

items.q: Why did the Pharisees complain at the feast in Levi's house?
o: Jesus' disciples ate with unwashed hands
Jesus ate with publicans and sinners
items.x: They asked, 'How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?'

items.q: Why did Joseph plan to put Mary away privily?
o: He had to move to Egypt
She was found with child before they came together
She had not paid her dowry
items.x: Being a just man and not willing to make her a public example, he was minded to put her away privily.

items.q: Why did the rich young man go away sorrowful?
o: He could not keep the commandments
items.x: Jesus told him to sell what he had and give to the poor. 'He went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions.'

items.q: Why did Jesus do not many mighty works in his own country?
o: Because Herod was searching for him
Because the people were sick of miracles
items.x: 'He did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.'

items.q: Which king was ruling Israel when Elijah announced there would be no rain?
items.x: Elijah told Ahab, 'There shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.'

items.q: Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up in the year which king died?
items.x: 'In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up.'

items.q: Which Persian king proclaimed that the Jews could return and build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem?
items.x: 'In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia', he made a proclamation to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.

items.q: Nehemiah was cupbearer to which king when he asked to rebuild Jerusalem?
items.x: 'In the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king ... I took up the wine, and gave it unto the king.'

items.q: Whose decree that all the world should be taxed sent Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem?
items.x: 'There went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.'

items.q: Luke dates John the Baptist's preaching to the fifteenth year of which emperor?
items.x: 'In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar ... the word of God came unto John.'

items.q: Which high priest told the council it was expedient that one man should die for the people?
items.x: Caiaphas, high priest that year, said this without knowing he was prophesying of Jesus' death.

items.q: After his arrest, Jesus was first led to which man, the father-in-law of the high priest?
items.x: 'And led him away to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas.'

items.q: An angel told her that her son would be a Nazarite from the womb. Who was her son?
items.x: The angel told Manoah's wife that no razor should come on his head. She called him Samson.

items.q: In which book does Hannah pray in the temple for a son?
items.x: Hannah prayed and vowed that if God gave her a son, she would give him to the LORD. Her son was Samuel.

items.q: Who was the last king of Judah, blinded and carried to Babylon?
items.x: They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, put out his eyes and carried him to Babylon.

items.q: Who brought the lad with five barley loaves and two small fishes to Jesus' attention?
items.x: 'Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, saith unto him, There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves.'

items.q: To whom did Jesus say, “Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more”?
o: The woman with an issue of blood
items.x: The scribes and Pharisees brought her to Jesus. When her accusers left, Jesus said this to her.

items.q: To whom did Jesus say, “Get thee behind me, Satan”?
items.x: Peter rebuked Jesus for foretelling his death. Jesus turned and said this to Peter.

items.q: Elijah told her, “make me thereof a little cake first.” Who was she?
items.x: She had only a handful of meal and a little oil, yet her barrel did not waste nor her cruse fail.

items.q: Who told Naaman's wife about the prophet in Samaria who could heal him?
o: A little maid taken captive from Israel
items.x: 'Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.'

items.q: Who sent a message to Pilate saying, “Have thou nothing to do with that just man”?
items.x: She said she had suffered many things in a dream because of him.

items.q: Jesus told the parable of the Good Samaritan to answer which question?
items.x: A lawyer, 'willing to justify himself', asked Jesus this, and Jesus answered with the parable.

items.q: When the prodigal son came home, what did his father have put on his hand?
items.x: 'Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.'

items.q: After talking with Jesus, what did the woman of Samaria leave behind at the well?
items.x: 'The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city.'

items.q: In the cave at Engedi, what did David secretly cut from King Saul?
items.x: David 'cut off the skirt of Saul's robe privily', and later his heart smote him for it.

items.q: The second time David spared Saul, what did he take from beside the sleeping king?
o: His spear and a cruse of water
items.x: 'David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster.'

items.q: How were Gideon's three hundred men chosen?
o: They lapped water with their hands to their mouths
items.x: The three hundred lapped, putting their hand to their mouth. The rest bowed down on their knees to drink.

items.q: What did God show Moses to throw into the bitter waters of Marah?
items.x: 'The LORD shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet.'

items.q: What did Achan confess he had hidden in his tent after Jericho?
o: A Babylonish garment, silver and gold
items.x: 'I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold.'

items.q: What did Samson first tell Delilah would make him weak?
o: Being bound with seven green withs
items.x: 'If they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak.'

items.q: Before praying on Mount Carmel, what did Elijah have poured over the sacrifice three times?
items.x: 'Fill four barrels with water, and pour it on the burnt sacrifice.' The water filled the trench too.

items.q: What did Elisha cast into the pot of poisoned stew to make it safe?
items.x: They cried, 'There is death in the pot.' Elisha said, 'Then bring meal,' and there was no harm in the pot.

items.q: What did the risen Jesus have ready on a fire of coals when the disciples came to shore?
items.x: 'They saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.'

items.q: What did the Good Samaritan pour into the wounded man's wounds?
items.x: He 'bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast.'

items.q: What did Peter see let down from heaven in his vision at Joppa?
o: A great sheet full of beasts
items.x: 'A certain vessel ... as it had been a great sheet', with all manner of fourfooted beasts.

items.q: Peter was lodging with Simon the tanner when Cornelius sent for him. In which town?
items.x: 'Send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter: he lodgeth with one Simon a tanner.'

items.q: What were Paul and Silas doing at midnight in the Philippian jail?
items.x: 'At midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.'

items.q: Which prophet was told to marry Gomer as a picture of Israel's unfaithfulness?
items.x: 'So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim.'

items.q: Which Gospel opens with “the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham”?
items.x: Matthew begins with Jesus' family line from Abraham through David.

items.q: Where was the tabernacle when young Samuel served the LORD under Eli?
items.x: Hannah brought Samuel to the house of the LORD in Shiloh, and there the LORD revealed himself to him.

items.q: After returning from Egypt, Joseph took Mary and Jesus to live in which town?
items.x: 'He came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled ... He shall be called a Nazarene.'

items.q: In Mark's Gospel, in whose house was Jesus anointed with an alabaster box of ointment?
items.x: 'Being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box.'

items.q: What did Jesus tell his hearers to do for those who despitefully use and persecute them?
items.x: 'Love your enemies ... and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.'

items.q: In the Lord's Prayer in Matthew, what comes right after “Give us this day our daily bread”?
o: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors
And lead us not into temptation
items.x: 'Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.'

items.q: In John 14, what does Jesus call the Holy Ghost whom the Father will send?
items.x: 'He shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever.'

items.q: Why did Rebekah send Jacob away to her brother Laban?
o: There was a famine in Canaan
items.x: Esau said, 'Then will I slay my brother Jacob.' Rebekah told Jacob, 'Flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran.'

items.q: Why did the Philistines send the ark of God back to Israel?
o: Their cities were struck with plagues
items.x: Wherever the ark went, the hand of God was heavy on the city. So they sent it back on a new cart.

items.q: Why did Ahab sulk and refuse to eat in his bed?
o: Naboth would not give him his vineyard
items.x: Ahab came home 'heavy and displeased' because Naboth would not give him the inheritance of his fathers.

items.q: Why did David send Uriah back to the battle with a letter for Joab?
o: To make peace with the Ammonites
To have Uriah killed in the fighting
items.x: 'Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle ... that he may be smitten, and die.'

items.q: Why did Mordecai refuse to bow to Haman, according to what he told the king's servants?
items.x: The servants asked why he would not bow, 'for he had told them that he was a Jew.'

items.q: Why couldn't Zacchaeus see Jesus through the crowd?
items.x: He sought to see Jesus, 'and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.'

items.q: Why did the four friends uncover the roof of the house where Jesus was teaching?
o: They could not reach him for the crowd
The man was too heavy to carry through
items.x: 'When they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof.'

items.q: Why did the boy Samuel keep running to Eli in the night?
o: He was afraid of the dark
He saw a vision of fire
He thought Eli was calling him
items.x: Samuel did not yet know the LORD, so he ran to Eli saying, 'Here am I; for thou calledst me.'

items.q: Why did Jesus say Mary of Bethany had chosen “that good part”?
o: She sat at his feet and heard his word
items.x: Mary 'sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word' while Martha served.

items.q: Why did Paul appeal to Caesar during his trial before Festus?
o: Festus wanted to send him to Jerusalem to be judged
He wanted to see Rome as a tourist
He had been sentenced to death
items.x: Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, asked Paul to go up to Jerusalem. Paul said, 'I appeal unto Caesar.'

items.q: Why did the people of Israel ask Samuel for a king?
o: The Philistines had captured the ark
His sons did not walk in his ways and they wanted to be like other nations
items.x: 'Thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.'

items.q: Why did Jesus overturn the tables of the money changers?
o: They had made God's house a den of thieves
items.x: 'It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.'

items.q: Why did Pilate send Jesus to Herod during the trial?
o: He learned Jesus was from Galilee, under Herod's rule
items.x: 'As soon as he knew that he belonged unto Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod.'

items.q: Who was the first of Jesus' disciples to reach the empty tomb, according to John?
o: The other disciple, whom Jesus loved
items.x: The other disciple 'did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre', though Peter went in first.

items.q: What sign did the angel give the shepherds to find the baby?
o: A bright star over the house
Wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger
items.x: 'Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger.'

items.q: What happened to Zacharias when he doubted the angel's message about John?
o: He was struck dumb until John was born
He went blind for three days
He was put out of the temple
items.x: 'Thou shalt be dumb, and not able to speak, until the day that these things shall be performed.'

items.q: What did Hezekiah do with the letter from the king of Assyria?
o: Spread it before the LORD in the temple
items.x: Hezekiah went up into the house of the LORD and spread the letter before the LORD.

items.q: When Saul and his servant looked for lost donkeys, whom did they end up meeting?
items.x: Saul was seeking his father's asses when he met Samuel, who anointed him king.

items.q: When Jesus heard Lazarus was sick, why did he say the sickness was not unto death?
o: It was for the glory of God
Jesus could heal from far away
items.x: 'This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God.' He then stayed two days where he was.

items.q: Why did the woman with the issue of blood touch Jesus' clothes?
o: She believed touching them would make her whole
She wanted to stop him leaving
She was trying to ask for money
items.x: 'For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.'

items.q: Besides the coat of many colours, what made Joseph's brothers hate him even more?
items.x: 'They hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.'

items.q: Why did Moses' mother hide him for three months?
o: The midwives were looking for him
Pharaoh ordered every Hebrew son cast into the river
items.x: Pharaoh commanded, 'Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river.' She saw he was a goodly child and hid him.

items.q: Why did Pharaoh's daughter name the baby Moses?
o: Because she drew him out of the water
items.x: 'She called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.'

items.q: Why did Nebuchadnezzar order the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual?
o: He was furious that the three Hebrews would not serve his gods
It had gone out the day before
He wanted to test a new furnace
items.x: 'Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury ... he commanded that they should heat the furnace one seven times more.'

items.q: How did King Darius spend the night Daniel was in the lions' den?
items.x: 'The king went to his palace, and passed the night fasting ... and his sleep went from him.'

items.q: What reason did David give for not killing Saul in the cave?
o: His men would turn on him
items.x: 'The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD's anointed.'

items.q: Why did Elijah flee into the wilderness after his victory on Mount Carmel?
o: God told him to hide from the drought
items.x: Jezebel sent word that by tomorrow his life would be as one of the dead prophets. 'He arose, and went for his life.'

items.q: Why did Jesus say, “Suffer the little children to come unto me”?
o: His disciples were rebuking those who brought them
The children's parents had left them
The Pharisees wanted the children sent home
items.x: 'His disciples rebuked those that brought them. But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased.'

items.q: Why were seven men like Stephen chosen in Acts 6?
o: Widows were being neglected in the daily ministration
items.x: The Grecians complained 'because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration.'

items.q: Why did Barnabas have to bring Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem?
o: Saul did not speak their language
The disciples were afraid of him
items.x: 'They were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple. But Barnabas took him.'

items.q: After washing the disciples' feet, what reason did Jesus give?
o: To prepare them for the passover
To give them an example to follow
To cleanse them from sin before the feast
items.x: 'For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.'

items.q: Why did the soldiers not break Jesus' legs on the cross?
items.x: They broke the legs of the two others, 'but when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs.'

items.q: After his dream at Bethel, what did Jacob do with the stone he had slept on?
o: Set it up for a pillar and poured oil on it
items.x: 'Jacob ... took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.'

items.q: Why did the LORD smite the men of Bethshemesh after the Philistines sent the ark back?
o: They touched it to steady the cart
They set it in a temple beside an idol
They kept the Philistines' golden gifts
items.x: 'He smote the men of Bethshemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the LORD.' (Uzzah touching the ark came later, in 2 Samuel 6.)

items.q: In the battle at Michmash, what did Jonathan do that put him under his father Saul's death oath?
o: He took spoil before the battle ended
items.x: Jonathan had not heard Saul's oath against eating. He dipped his rod in an honeycomb; later the people rescued him from death.

items.q: Why was Naaman angry at first when he came to Elisha's house to be healed?
o: Elisha asked for a large payment
Elisha only sent a messenger out to him
Elisha told him to go back to Syria
items.x: Elisha sent a messenger to say 'wash in Jordan seven times'. Naaman was wroth: 'I thought, He will surely come out to me.'

items.q: Why did Paul and Barnabas part ways before Paul's second missionary journey?
o: They disagreed about taking John Mark
Barnabas was called back to Jerusalem
Paul wanted to go to Rome first
items.x: Mark had left them at Pamphylia. 'The contention was so sharp between them' that Barnabas took Mark to Cyprus and Paul chose Silas.

items.q: At Philippi, why was the keeper of the prison about to kill himself?
o: He had beaten innocent Roman citizens
The earthquake had killed his family
He thought the prisoners had fled
He feared the magistrates for believing Paul
items.x: After the earthquake opened every door, he 'drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.'

items.q: Mark says Jesus found 'nothing but leaves' on the fig tree he cursed. What detail does Mark add?
o: It had been dug about and dunged
It grew on a rock by the wayside
It was not yet the time of figs
It had borne no fruit for three years
items.x: 'He found nothing but leaves; for the time of figs was not yet.' The 'three years' and 'dig about it, and dung it' are from Jesus' parable in Luke 13.

items.q: What were Belshazzar and his guests drinking from on the night of the writing on the wall?
o: Cups made from the idols of Babylon
The gold and silver vessels from the temple in Jerusalem
The cups of Daniel and his friends
items.x: Belshazzar commanded to bring 'the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem'.

items.q: What did Joshua and the princes of Israel fail to do before making a league with the Gibeonites?
o: Read them the law of Moses
items.x: The Gibeonites claimed to come 'from a far country'. 'The men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD.'

items.q: David prayed, 'Turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.' Whose advice did Absalom follow instead?
items.x: 'The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel.'

items.q: On the night King Ahasuerus could not sleep, what did he find out?
o: Mordecai had saved his life and was never rewarded
Haman had built a gallows for Mordecai
The Jews were to be destroyed by his own decree
items.x: The chronicles were read: Mordecai had reported Bigthana and Teresh's plot, and 'There is nothing done for him.'

items.q: When wicked Athaliah killed the royal family, where was the baby Joash hidden for six years?
o: In the house of the LORD
In the palace of the king of Egypt
items.x: Jehosheba stole Joash away; 'he was with her hid in the house of the LORD six years. And Athaliah did reign over the land.'

items.q: Zacchaeus promised to give half his goods to the poor. What did he promise anyone he had wronged by false accusation?
o: To repay him with a fifth added
items.x: 'If I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.'

items.q: The mark God set on Cain was meant to protect him from being killed.
items.x: 'The LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.'

items.q: The Bible says Saul fell off his horse on the road to Damascus.
items.x: No horse is mentioned. A light shone round about him 'and he fell to the earth'.

items.q: It was the angel Gabriel who appeared to Joseph in a dream.
items.x: Matthew says 'the angel of the Lord' appeared to Joseph. Gabriel is named when he was sent to Mary.

items.q: The book of Genesis names the serpent in Eden as Satan.
items.x: Genesis only says 'the serpent'. It is Revelation that calls the devil 'that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan'.

items.q: “Sir, we would see Jesus.”
items.x: Greeks who came up to worship at the Passover asked Philip, who told Andrew, and they told Jesus.

items.q: “Should such a man as I flee? and who is there, that, being as I am, would go into the temple to save his life?”
items.x: False prophets urged Nehemiah to hide in the temple from his enemies. He refused: 'I will not go in.'

items.q: “Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards?”
items.x: Elisha said this to Gehazi, who had secretly taken silver and garments from Naaman.

items.q: “Blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood.”
items.x: David said it to Abigail, whose gifts and wise words stopped him from taking revenge on her husband Nabal.

items.q: “Spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.”
items.x: At the threshing floor Ruth asked Boaz to act as her near kinsman.

items.q: “Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy?”
items.x: The king of Israel tore his clothes when he read the Syrian king's letter about Naaman; Elisha then sent for Naaman.

items.q: After crossing the Red Sea, put these places Israel came to in order.
items.x: Bitter waters at Marah, twelve wells at Elim, manna in the wilderness of Sin, then Sinai in the third month.

items.q: Put these places in Elijah's story in order.
items.x: Fed by ravens at Cherith, the widow at Zarephath, fire on Carmel, then forty days' journey to Horeb.

items.q: Samson killed the young lion with his bare hands.
items.x: 'The Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand.'

items.q: Two of Jesus' twelve apostles were named James.
items.x: 'James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother' and 'James the son of Alphaeus'.

clues: On the prophet's word I left my home for seven years during a famine and lived among the Philistines.
When my only son died, I laid him on the prophet's bed and rode to find the man of God.
My husband and I built a little chamber on the wall for a holy man to stay in.
I was a great woman of Shunem who always gave Elisha a meal when he passed by.
o: The widow with the pot of oil
items.x: The Shunammite woman housed Elisha; he promised her a son and later raised him from the dead.

items.q: Put these events in Nehemiah's story in order.
o: He hears that Jerusalem's wall is broken down
He asks the king to send him to Judah
The wall is finished in fifty-two days
He views the walls by night
items.x: Bad news in Shushan (1:3), his request to Artaxerxes (2:5), the night inspection (2:13), then the wall finished in 52 days (6:15).

clues: My ships of Tharshish were broken at Eziongeber before they could sail for gold.
At Ramothgilead I went into battle in my royal robes while the king of Israel disguised himself.
Before one battle I appointed singers to go out in front of the army praising the LORD.
I was a king of Judah who joined affinity with Ahab.
items.x: Jehoshaphat, a godly king of Judah, allied with Ahab and later saw God win a battle while his singers praised.

clues: While Jerusalem was under siege, I bought my cousin's field in Anathoth.
I was let down with cords into a dungeon and sank in the mire.
An Ethiopian named Ebedmelech had me pulled out of the dungeon.
When God called me, I said, 'Behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.'
items.x: Jeremiah, the 'weeping prophet', was called young and suffered for warning Judah before Babylon took Jerusalem.

clues: I despised my husband in my heart when I saw him leaping and dancing before the LORD.
I laid an image in a bed with a pillow of goats' hair to fool my father's messengers.
I let my husband down through a window so he could escape.
I was King Saul's daughter, given to David as his wife.
items.x: Michal, Saul's daughter, saved David from her father's men but later despised him for dancing before the ark.

clues: I told King Hezekiah's servants to lay a lump of figs on his boil.
I walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign against Egypt and Ethiopia.
A seraph touched my lips with a live coal from the altar.
When the Lord asked, 'Whom shall I send?', I answered, 'Here am I; send me.'
items.x: Isaiah saw the Lord in the temple, answered his call, and later advised King Hezekiah.

clues: An arrow shot 'at a venture' found the joints of my armour, and dogs licked up my blood at Samaria.
I called a prophet 'he that troubleth Israel'.
I lay on my bed and would eat no bread because a man refused to sell me his vineyard.
My wife was Jezebel.
items.x: Ahab, king of Israel, married Jezebel, opposed Elijah, coveted Naboth's vineyard, and died in battle at Ramothgilead.

clues: When I heard Jesus was coming after my brother died, I went out to meet him while my sister sat in the house.
I was cumbered about much serving.
I complained to Jesus that my sister had left me to serve alone.
I lived at Bethany with my sister Mary and my brother Lazarus.
items.x: Martha of Bethany served Jesus, complained about Mary, and met Jesus before he raised Lazarus.

items.q: In the synagogue at Nazareth, Jesus angered the crowd by reminding them of which two Old Testament stories?
o: Elijah and the widow of Sarepta, and Naaman the Syrian
Jonah at Nineveh, and the queen of the south
David eating the shewbread, and Abiathar the priest
Moses' brasen serpent, and the manna
items.x: God sent Elias only to a widow of Sarepta, and cleansed only Naaman the Syrian, both outsiders. The crowd tried to 'cast him down headlong'.

items.q: Three of David's mighty men broke through the Philistines to bring him water from the well of Bethlehem. Why would he not drink it?
o: The Philistines had poisoned the well
He saw it as the blood of men who risked their lives
He had vowed to fast until the battle was won
The priest said it was unclean
items.x: He poured it out unto the LORD: 'is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives?'

items.q: Goliath had a brother who was also killed by one of David's warriors.
items.x: 'Elhanan the son of Jair slew Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, whose spear staff was like a weaver's beam.'

items.q: People laid the sick in the streets hoping Peter's shadow would fall on them as he passed.
items.x: 'That at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them.' (Handkerchiefs and aprons were carried from Paul, Acts 19:12.)

items.text: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls:

There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;

This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.
Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

items.q: What 'proof' did the Gibeonites show Joshua to make him think they came from a far country?
o: A letter sealed by their king
Dry, mouldy bread and worn-out sacks and shoes
Camels lame from the long road
Coins from a land Joshua had never seen
items.x: 'All the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy', with old sacks, rent wine bottles and old shoes. Gibeon was actually close by.

items.q: When Jacob fled from Laban, what did Rachel steal and then hide by sitting on it?
items.x: Rachel stole Laban's images, put them in the camel's furniture and sat on them while Laban searched the tent.

items.q: Why did the Israelites in Saul's day have to go down to the Philistines to sharpen their ploughshares and axes?
o: The Philistines let no smith work in Israel, so Israel couldn't make swords
The Philistines owned all the grinding stones
The law of Moses forbade smiths in the camp
items.x: 'There was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears.' At the battle only Saul and Jonathan had a sword.

items.q: On the day of Pentecost, how did some mockers explain the disciples speaking in other tongues?
o: They said the men had studied in Egypt
They said the men were full of new wine
They said the men had devils
They said the men were reading from scrolls
items.x: 'Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine.' Peter answered that it was only the third hour of the day.

items.q: Why did King Saul go looking for a woman with a familiar spirit at Endor?
o: The LORD would not answer him by dreams, Urim or prophets
Samuel had told him to go to her
He wanted a curse put on David
items.x: 'The LORD answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.' Then Saul said, 'Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit.'

items.q: When Jesus asked the man with the unclean spirit his name in Mark 5, what was the answer?
items.x: 'My name is Legion: for we are many.' The spirits were then sent into a herd of swine.

items.q: What did the five daughters of Zelophehad ask Moses for?
o: Husbands from the tribe of Judah
Their father's inheritance, since he had no sons
Permission to serve at the tabernacle
Their father's body to bury in Canaan
items.x: Their father died with no sons, so they asked, 'Give unto us therefore a possession among the brethren of our father.' God said they spoke right.

items.q: When men of the tribe of Dan passed Micah's house on their way north, what did they take?
o: His carved image, ephod and teraphim, and his priest
items.x: They fetched the carved image, the ephod and the teraphim, and talked Micah's Levite into being priest to a whole tribe.

items.q: How does 2 Kings end, after Jerusalem has fallen?
o: Babylon's new king frees Jehoiachin and feeds him at his table
Cyrus lets the Jews go home
Daniel is made ruler over Babylon
items.x: Evilmerodach lifted up Jehoiachin out of prison, spoke kindly to him, and he ate bread before the king all his life. A small sign of hope.

items.q: What exactly was the lie of Ananias and Sapphira?
o: They claimed to have healed a lame man
They gave money they had stolen
They kept back part of the price of their land
They said they had seen the risen Lord
items.x: They sold a possession and 'kept back part of the price', bringing only part to the apostles as if it were all.

items.q: What did Simon the sorcerer try to buy from Peter and John?
o: The power to give the Holy Ghost by laying on hands
A place among the twelve apostles
The secret of healing the lame
A scroll of the prophet Isaiah
items.x: 'He offered them money, saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost.'

items.q: In Ezra's time, what did the prophets Haggai and Zechariah stir the Jews to get on with?
o: Building the house of God in Jerusalem
items.x: After they prophesied, Zerubbabel and Jeshua 'began to build the house of God which is at Jerusalem'. The wall came later, under Nehemiah.

items.q: According to 1 Chronicles, why was David not allowed to build the temple?
o: He had shed much blood and made great wars
He was not from the tribe of Levi
items.x: 'Thou hast shed blood abundantly, and hast made great wars: thou shalt not build an house unto my name.' Solomon built it.

items.q: Why did Jesus send Peter to catch a fish in Matthew 17?
o: A coin in its mouth would pay the tribute for both of them
To show the disciples where to cast the net
To feed the crowd at Capernaum
As a sign for the Pharisees who asked for one
items.x: Asked if their master paid tribute, Jesus said 'lest we should offend them', open the first fish's mouth and 'thou shalt find a piece of money'.

items.q: After the fire fell on Carmel, Elijah ran ahead of King Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel.
items.x: 'The hand of the LORD was on Elijah; and he girded up his loins, and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.'

items.q: The word 'prodigal' appears in Jesus' parable of the son who wasted his inheritance.
items.x: The KJV never uses 'prodigal' there. The son 'wasted his substance with riotous living'; the title came later.

items.q: John's Gospel says it was Mary Magdalene who wiped Jesus' feet with her hair at Bethany.
items.x: John names Mary of Bethany, the sister of Martha and Lazarus: 'Then took Mary a pound of ointment... and wiped his feet with her hair.'

items.q: Samson's riddle came from honey he found in the carcase of a bear.
items.x: It was a lion: 'a swarm of bees and honey in the carcase of the lion'. Hence 'Out of the eater came forth meat'.

items.q: The Gospels give no hint that Peter was ever married.
items.x: Jesus came into Peter's house and 'saw his wife’s mother laid, and sick of a fever', so Peter had a wife.

items.q: Matthias took Judas's place among the twelve after the disciples cast lots.
items.x: 'They gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.'

items.q: When Jerusalem's officials asked the Assyrian Rabshakeh to speak in Syrian, he shouted even louder in the Jews' language.
items.x: He wanted the people on the wall to hear, so he 'cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language'.

items.q: Nehemiah's enemy Tobiah mocked that even a fox could break down the wall the Jews were building.
items.x: 'Tobiah the Ammonite... said, Even that which they build, if a fox go up, he shall even break down their stone wall.'

clues: My dying father said I was 'unstable as water' and would not excel.
In Egypt's famine I offered my own two sons as a pledge to bring Benjamin back.
I talked my brothers out of killing the dreamer and into using a pit, planning to rescue him.
I was Jacob's firstborn son.
items.x: Reuben meant to bring Joseph back to his father, but while he was away the brothers sold him.

clues: My sons Joel and Abiah took bribes, so the elders asked for a king.
I set up a stone between Mizpeh and Shen and named it Ebenezer.
As a boy I kept running to the old priest at night, sure he had called me.
My mother Hannah prayed for me and then lent me to the LORD.
items.x: Samuel was the last judge and the prophet who anointed both Saul and David.

clues: I told the king to go ahead and build God a house, then came back with a different word that same night.
With Bathsheba I made sure Solomon, not Adonijah, would sit on the throne.
I told the king a story about a rich man who took a poor man's one little ewe lamb.
I was the prophet who said to David, 'Thou art the man.'
items.x: Nathan served David as prophet through the temple promise, the Bathsheba sin and Solomon's rise.

clues: I threw a javelin at the young harpist who played to calm me.
Tired of waiting for Samuel, I offered the burnt offering myself.
When they came to make me king, I had hidden myself among the stuff.
I was a Benjamite, taller than everyone from my shoulders up, and Israel's first king.
items.x: King Saul started well but lost the kingdom through disobedience.

clues: My son-in-law said I changed his wages ten times.
I chased him for seven days and caught up with him in mount Gilead.
On the wedding night I gave him my elder daughter instead of the younger.
My nephew Jacob served me seven years for my daughter Rachel.
items.x: Laban was Rebekah's brother; he tricked Jacob with Leah and was outwitted in turn.

clues: When some Greeks asked to see Jesus, Philip came to me and we told Jesus together.
My home city Bethsaida was also the city of Philip.
I heard John the Baptist speak and followed Jesus that day.
The first thing I did was find my brother Simon Peter and bring him to Jesus.
items.x: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, keeps bringing people to Jesus in John's Gospel.

clues: My two Hittite wives were a grief of mind to my parents.
Years later I came with four hundred men to meet my brother, then ran and kissed him.
I wept and asked my father, 'Hast thou but one blessing?'
I was born red and hairy and grew up a cunning hunter.
items.x: Esau lost the birthright and the blessing to his twin Jacob, yet forgave him.

items.q: “my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions”
items.x: Rehoboam followed the young men's advice instead of the elders', and ten tribes broke away to Jeroboam.

items.q: “I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf”
items.x: Aaron's excuse to Moses for the golden calf. Exodus 32:4 says he fashioned it with a graving tool.

items.q: “I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart”
items.x: David's eldest brother Eliab, angry when David came to the battle with Goliath.

items.q: “What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?”
items.x: Judah, who then suggested selling Joseph to the Ishmeelites. Reuben had earlier argued for the pit.

items.q: “If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.”
items.x: Barak to Deborah. She went, but told him the honour would go to a woman: Jael killed Sisera.

items.q: “O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it.”
items.x: Before Solomon, the true mother would rather lose her son than see him divided. That is how Solomon knew.

items.q: Put these events of Saul's first days in Damascus in order.
o: Ananias lays his hands on him
Disciples let him down by the wall in a basket
He is led by the hand into Damascus, unable to see
He preaches Christ in the synagogues
items.x: Blind for three days, healed through Ananias, preaching straight away, then a night escape from a plot.

items.q: Put these events from the book of Ruth in order.
o: Ruth gleans in a field belonging to Boaz
Boaz calls ten elders to the city gate
Naomi's husband Elimelech dies in Moab
Ruth uncovers Boaz's feet at the threshing floor
items.x: Loss in Moab, gleaning at harvest, the night at the threshing floor, then Boaz settles the matter with the nearer kinsman before ten elders.

items.q: Put these events from the book of Esther in order.
o: Queen Vashti refuses to come at the king's command
Pur, the lot, is cast before Haman
Mordecai uncovers a plot against the king
items.x: Vashti refused, Esther was crowned, Mordecai reported the two chamberlains, then Haman cast lots to pick a day against the Jews.

items.text: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;
And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
And I sent messengers unto them, saying, I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down: why should the work cease, whilst I leave it, and come down to you?

Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.
And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.

For who hath despised the day of small things? for they shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven; they are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth.
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.

items.q: What did God send to wither the gourd that was shading Jonah?
items.x: God prepared a gourd for shade, then a worm that struck it so it withered in the sun.

items.q: On the first night of his fleece test, what did Gideon ask God for?
o: Fire to burn the offering on the rock
Dew only on the fleece, with the ground dry
Rain to fall on the threshing floor
A sign written in the sand
items.x: He asked for a wet fleece and dry ground, then asked for the reverse the next night.

items.q: Why did King Uzziah become leprous?
o: He went into the temple to burn incense himself
He refused to pay the temple tax
He married a priest's daughter from Moab
items.x: A priest tried to stop him at the altar, and the leprosy broke out on his forehead.

items.q: What did Naaman's servants point out when he was angry at Elisha's simple instruction?
o: That the Jordan was too muddy to bathe in
If the prophet had asked for something great, Naaman would have done it, so why not this simple thing?
That the king of Syria had forbidden the bath
items.x: Naaman expected a big gesture. His servants reasoned that a simple command was no reason to refuse.

items.q: What did the donkey see that Balaam could not?
o: A lion waiting in the vineyard
The angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword
A flood rising from the river
A cloud of smoke over the altar
items.x: Balaam beat the donkey three times for turning aside, unaware that the angel was there.

items.q: Why was Elisha angry with King Joash after Joash shot the arrow of deliverance?
o: Joash struck the ground only three times instead of five or six
Joash shot the arrow at the wrong city
Joash had not brought a bow
items.x: Elisha had told him to strike the ground, and Joash stopped early, so Syria would be beaten only partly.

items.q: Before Peter stepped out of the boat, what single word had Jesus said to him?
items.x: Peter walked on the water toward Jesus, until he saw the wind and began to sink.

items.q: Why did the Queen of Sheba travel to Jerusalem to see Solomon?
o: To test him with hard questions
To buy cedar from Lebanon for her king
To ask him to end a war with Egypt
To marry him and rule two lands
items.x: She had heard of his fame and came to test his wisdom. Then she praised God for him.

items.q: Which request did Jabez make to God?
o: A son to inherit the kingdom
Rain on his fields in a drought
To be blessed indeed, have his border enlarged, and be kept from evil
items.x: A short prayer in a long list of names. God granted what he asked.

items.q: What did Melchizedek bring out to Abram after his victory?
items.x: Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High, and he blessed Abram.

items.q: A man who had killed someone by accident fled to a city of refuge. From whom was he protected there?
items.x: Refuge cities were for accidental killers, so they could stand trial before the congregation.

items.q: What had Israel been burning incense to, until King Hezekiah broke it in pieces?
o: A golden calf from the wilderness
An idol shaped like a dove
The bronze serpent Moses had made
items.x: Hezekiah smashed it because the people had been treating it as an object of worship.

items.q: What did Paul find in Athens that he used as his starting point?
o: A statue of Hermes in the marketplace
A temple of Artemis with silver shrines
A scroll of the law of Moses
An altar inscribed 'To the unknown God'
items.x: Paul said he had seen their devotions and found an altar with that inscription.

items.q: After the contest on Carmel, what did Jezebel vow to do to Elijah?
o: Burn his house with him inside
Send him to Egypt in chains
Kill him by the next day
items.x: Elijah ran into the wilderness afterward.

items.q: Jonah was swallowed by a whale.
items.x: Jesus said 'the whale's belly'. Jonah 1:17 only says 'a great fish'.

items.q: The sun stood still for Elijah during his battle on Mount Carmel.
items.x: The sun stood still for Joshua at Gibeon, until the people had avenged themselves. Elijah had no such day.

items.q: Pharaoh restored both his cupbearer and his baker to their posts.
items.x: The cupbearer got his job back. The baker was hanged, as Joseph had interpreted.

items.q: Moses went up Mount Sinai with the people following him to the top.
items.x: God told Moses to set bounds so the people would not come up the mount.

items.q: Samson's strength was tied to the uncut hair of his head.
items.x: He told Delilah his strength would go if his head was shaven, and it did.

items.q: Paul was bitten by a viper on Malta and suffered no harm.
