items.x: The islanders expected him to swell up dead. He shook the beast off into the fire.

items.q: Ruth was an Israelite by birth who moved to Moab.
items.x: Ruth was a Moabitess who married into Naomi's family and came back to Bethlehem with her.

items.q: The wise men came to the manger the night Jesus was born.
items.x: Matthew says they came into the house, and the child was a young child by then.

clues: Men said my counsel was as if they had asked God himself.
I hanged myself when my advice was overturned.
I advised Absalom to go in to his father's concubines on the roof, in full view of Israel.
I was David's counsellor until my plan was turned to foolishness.
items.x: Absalom followed his advice on the roof, then Hushai's counsel beat his plan.

clues: My refusal made the king's advisers fear every wife in the land would copy me.
The king sent his servants to bring me to his feast, and I would not come.
The king wanted me to show my beauty to his guests.
I was queen of Persia until the king replaced me.
items.x: She refused the king's summons at a banquet, and her crown went to Esther.

clues: A woman's hand ended my life with a tent peg.
I had nine hundred chariots of iron and oppressed Israel for twenty years.
I fled on foot to a tent, asked for water, and got milk.
I was the captain of King Jabin's army.
items.x: Jael was the wife of Heber, and she gave him milk before killing him.

clues: I escaped a massacre of my father's priestly house and fled to David.
I carried the ephod down to David when he hid at Keilah.
I was the priest who threw in with Adonijah when Solomon was crowned.
I was a son of the priest Ahimelech.
items.x: He backed Adonijah's bid for the throne, and Solomon sent him away to Anathoth.

clues: God's anger burned against me and my two friends for not speaking rightly of Job.
A spirit passed before my face in a night vision and made my hair stand up.
I was the first of Job's three friends to speak.
I was one of the three friends who came to comfort Job.
items.x: He called on Job to remember that the innocent do not perish, based on a vision.

clues: The man who killed me was the one I was chasing.
I was as light of foot as a wild roe.
I was a son of Zeruiah and a brother of Joab.
items.x: He would not turn from Abner, and Abner killed him with the back of his spear.

clues: The hilt went in after the blade, and my fat closed over it.
For eighteen years Israel served me.
I was a very fat man.
I was king of Moab.
items.x: Ehud came to deliver tribute, then killed him in his summer parlour.

items.q: “The LORD forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.”
items.x: The king wanted his neighbour's vineyard for a garden. The answer was a flat no, and it was about family land.

items.q: “but these sheep, what have they done?”
items.x: David saw the angel of the plague and asked that the punishment fall on him and his house instead.

items.q: “Let me go, for the day breaketh.”
items.x: The man wrestling at the ford of Jabbok wanted to leave at dawn. Jacob would not let him go without a blessing.

items.q: “yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!”
items.x: He said preaching was not a choice for him. It was laid on him.

items.q: “I do well to be angry, even unto death.”
items.x: He said this about the withered gourd, after God asked him if his anger was right.

items.q: “Is it well with the child?”
items.x: He sent his servant to ask about the boy before he went to the house himself.

items.q: Put these events of Jacob's deception in order.
o: Isaac smells Jacob's garments and blesses him
Esau vows to kill Jacob after their father dies
Esau returns with his savoury meat
Rebekah sends Jacob away to Laban
items.x: The blessing came first, then Esau's failed hunt, then the vow, then the escape.

items.q: Put these events at Jericho in order.
o: The city is burned with fire
Joshua sends the spies to Rahab's house
Rahab and her household are brought out
items.x: The wall fell after the shout, the spies got Rahab out, then the city burned.

items.q: Put these events of Elijah on Carmel in order.
o: Fire falls on the sacrifice soaked with water
A little cloud rises out of the sea
The people fall on their faces
Elijah has the prophets of Baal slain at the brook
items.x: The fire first, then the people's confession, then the slaughter, then the rain.

items.q: What small sign did Elijah's servant see rising from the sea after the long drought?
o: A cloud the size of a man's hand
A pillar of smoke over Samaria
A flock of birds over the Jordan
items.x: A little cloud rose from the sea, and the rain followed soon after.

items.q: What did King Jehoiakim do with Baruch's scroll after three or four leaves had been read?
o: He sealed it with his ring and buried it
He cut it with a penknife and threw it into the fire
He gave it to the priests to hide
He read the rest of it aloud at midnight
items.x: He would not listen, and burned the whole roll, so Jeremiah wrote it again.

items.q: When Samson woke after Delilah cut his hair, what did he not know?
o: The LORD had departed from him
The Philistines had already sold his armour
The gates of Gaza had been locked against him
Delilah had hidden his strength in a jar
items.x: He went out as before, but his strength had gone.

items.q: Who did young Samuel first think was calling him in the night?
items.x: Three times he ran to the old priest before the penny dropped.

items.q: What did Daniel tell Belshazzar had been weighed in the balances?
o: The gold cups from the temple
The king himself, and he was found wanting
items.x: The writing on the wall was read as numbered, weighed, and divided.

items.q: Esther's resolve to go in to the king uninvited ends with what words?
o: Let the king decide my fate
Then the LORD will see me through
Tell Mordecai to keep watch at the gate
items.x: She asked the Jews to fast with her for three days, then she went in.

items.q: How did the people on Paul's ship reach land when it broke up off Malta?
o: Some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship
They swam one by one through the surf
They rode on the backs of dolphins
A Roman galley carried them all
items.x: Everyone got to land, just as the angel had promised, but the ship did not.

items.q: What did the widow of Zarephath say she had left in the house?
o: An handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruse
A jar of wine and a loaf of bread
Two sheep and a measure of barley
A chest of figs and a jug of honey
items.x: Elijah told her not to fear, and her jars did not run dry.

items.q: When the prodigal son was starving among the pigs, what 'came to him'?
o: A letter from his older brother
A vision of the angels of heaven
A bag of silver from a stranger
items.x: He worked out that his father's servants had more than he did.

items.q: Where was Jesus when the storm rose on the lake?
o: On the shore under a fig tree
In a tent on the mountain
Standing on the nets at the bow
Asleep on a pillow in the back of the boat
items.x: The disciples woke him up, and he calmed the sea with one word.

items.q: What happened to a dead man who was thrown into Elisha's grave and touched the prophet's bones?
o: He came back to life and stood on his feet
He was carried to the priests for a blessing
He was buried under the altar in Gilgal
He shouted for the prophet to come back
items.x: The body touched Elisha's bones, and the man revived and got up on his feet.

items.q: What turns away wrath, according to Proverbs 15:1?
o: A long silence before the crowd
A loud warning from the walls
items.x: The sharp word stirs anger; the gentle one turns it.

items.q: Which fruit of the Spirit is listed first in Galatians 5:22?
items.x: Joy and peace come after it in the list.

items.q: How long did Methuselah live, according to Genesis 5:27?
items.x: The oldest man in the Bible, and he died the year of the flood.

items.q: Jonah preached in Nineveh for forty years before the city repented.
items.x: Jonah walked in and gave the city forty days' warning; the king's city repented in those days.

items.q: Uzzah was struck dead for touching the ark of God to steady it.
items.x: Uzzah reached out to steady the ark when the oxen stumbled, and God's anger broke out on him.

items.q: In Eden, the serpent walked on legs before God cursed it.
items.x: God says the serpent goes on its belly; the Bible never gives it legs before the curse.

items.q: While the ark stayed in his house, the LORD blessed the household of Obed-edom.
items.x: The ark stayed three months at his house, and the family prospered.

items.q: Hanun shaved off half of David's servants' beards.
items.x: Hanun the Ammonite insulted David's messengers, and the war that followed began with that shame.

items.q: Solomon's temple was built with the ringing of iron hammers across Jerusalem.
items.x: The stones were prepared at the quarry, so no hammer or axe or iron tool was heard in the house while it was built.

items.q: Paul was struck down on the road to Damascus by a voice that spoke to him in Greek.
items.x: The voice spoke in the Hebrew tongue, Paul says, not in Greek.

items.q: Daniel's three friends came out of the furnace smelling of smoke.
items.x: The king's princes saw that their hair was not singed and their coats were not changed, and the smell of fire had not passed on them.

clues: I was killed on the same day as my brother, and the ark was taken from Israel.
I took meat for the priest before the fat was burned, and the people despised the LORD's offering.
My father was the judge in Shiloh, and I was one of his sons who knew not the LORD.
I was a son of Eli, a priest who did wickedly in the tabernacle at Shiloh.
items.x: Eli's sons took the best parts of the offerings. Both died in the battle when the ark was taken.

clues: Paul went up to Jerusalem with me, and I was a Greek, yet I was not made to be circumcised.
I was sent to Corinth, and my coming comforted Paul in Macedonia.
Paul left me in Crete to set things in order.
I am a true son of Paul in the common faith.
items.x: Paul's companion in the Gentile mission, sent with the collection to Corinth.

clues: The Jews thought Paul had brought me into the temple, and they cried out against him.
I was an Ephesian who travelled with Paul from Greece to Jerusalem.
I was left sick at Miletum.
I was one of Paul's companions from Asia to Jerusalem.
items.x: A companion from Ephesus whose presence in Jerusalem caused a riot.

clues: I hid a royal child in the temple for six years while a queen ruled the land.
I was the priest who commanded the captains to guard the boy king.
I anointed Joash and crowned him, then the people shouted at Athaliah's death.
